contract.note: identical raw-waveform contract to the non-streaming Moonshine port, so the frontend is reusable

export.graphs: encoder, cross-attention projection and autoregressive decoder step
export.note: headDim 40 against 36 on the non-streaming checkpoint, which exposed a hardcoded-geometry bug in the pair runner
export.validity: INVALID. The exported streaming encoder was built from randomly initialized weights, so the graphs do not represent this checkpoint. They are retained only as evidence of what was attempted and must not be used.

runner_fix: the runner now reads slots, heads and headDim from the export receipt instead of constants, so it is no longer pinned to one checkpoint

decode_result.symptom: 256 tokens with a repeating pair and no EOS
decode_result.reading: a streaming-trained decoder fed whole-utterance encoder states is out of distribution; chunked decoding with the model's own right-context convention is required and was not built

oracle_blocked.error: ValueError: text input must be of type str, list[str] or list[list[str]]
oracle_blocked.stage: inside model.generate, so the installed transformers cannot run generate for this checkpoint
oracle_blocked.consequence: no reference transcript exists, so the port cannot be gated

not_done: chunked streaming decode loop with the model's context convention
a reference transcript, blocked on the transformers generate failure
honest_note: download and export succeeded and the graphs load and run; the model does not yet transcribe. Nothing here supports a claim about accuracy or streaming quality.

root_cause.finding: the checkpoint stores the encoder under model.encoder.embedder.conv1.weight and siblings, while the non-streaming checkpoint stores model.encoder.conv1.weight directly
root_cause.consequence: the installed transformers maps none of the streaming encoder tensors, loads the model anyway, and randomly initializes the whole encoder. It reports this only as a warning, and generation then emits repeated filler.
root_cause.evidence: load reported newly initialized model.encoder.conv1.weight, conv2, conv3, groupnorm, layer_norm and every layer's input_layernorm and post_attention_layernorm; the checkpoint key census shows model.encoder.embedder.* and model.model.encoder.conv1.* for the non-streaming model
root_cause.oracle_consequence: no reference transcript can be produced with this toolchain, so nothing can be gated
root_cause.silent_success_class: a load that succeeds, produces plausible-shaped output and only warns. The same class as the dead cross-attention input and the data-section-relative offsets earlier in this session.

definitive_finding.measured: loading the remapped state dict fails hard with a shape mismatch: checkpoint conv1 is [640, 320, 5] while the installed model expects [320, 1, 127]
definitive_finding.meaning: the streaming encoder consumes 320-dimensional features with a 5-tap convolution kernel, where the non-streaming encoder consumes raw 16 kHz waveform through a single channel with a 127-tap kernel
definitive_finding.frontend_consequence: this checkpoint needs a mel frontend that the non-streaming port does not have. The published preprocessor_config.json describes a Wav2Vec2FeatureExtractor with do_normalize false, which does not match a 320-bin mel encoder, so the repository's own processor config does not describe this model's input either
definitive_finding.conclusion: the streaming checkpoint is a different model, not a renamed one. No key mapping can bridge a different subsampler, and the installed transformers has no class for it.
definitive_finding.prerequisite: the streaming Moonshine architecture together with its mel frontend, from a transformers version that ships it, or hand-written support
corrections_made: an intermediate reading claimed the encoder lacked conv modules and relative_k_proj, so a rename could not work; a full key comparison refuted that
the follow-up claim that a rename was sufficient was then refuted by the shape mismatch above
the recorded finding is the measured shape mismatch, which is what survives

prerequisites: the streaming Moonshine architecture and its 320-bin mel frontend; the installed transformers has no class for it
then re-export, then produce a reference transcript, then gate
runner_fix_still_valid: the pair runner now reads slots, heads and headDim from the export receipt rather than constants; that fix stands independently of this checkpoint
artifacts: the remap tool is kept at tools/moonshine-onnx-export/remap_streaming_state_dict.py because the 19 key renames it performs are real and would be needed for any future streaming class, but it does not and cannot fix this checkpoint

community_onnx_evaluated.finding: community ONNX exports of moonshine-streaming do exist: Mazino0/moonshine-streaming-small-onnx, Mazino0/moonshine-streaming-medium-onnx, Immortalizer/moonshine-streaming-small-onnx and felixem/moonshine-streaming-tiny-optimized
community_onnx_evaluated.no_official_export: onnx-community ships onnx exports for the non-streaming Moonshine models but none for the streaming ones; the three official-looking ids probed returned HTTP 401
reasons: unknown provenance, and this project exports its own graphs from official weights

the same failure already cost this project once: the browser graphs shipped for non-streaming Moonshine carried a different checkpoint revision and drifted from PyTorch by more than 1.6 in encoder output while still producing a correct transcript on one fixture
a third-party graph would still need the mel frontend reverse-engineered from the graph, which is the unresolved blocker either way
community_onnx_evaluated.note: this is a recorded decision, not an oversight; revisiting it means accepting unverified upstream weights
